extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly — educated general readers, scientists, students, and professionals seeking reviews of scientific, philosophical, and technical books
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used in a late-19th-century popular-science magazine to evaluate and recommend scientific, technical, philosophical, and travel/guide books; emphasizes style, scholarship, usefulness, structure, illustrations, and physical production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular exposition qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: A work intended for the general public should be "popular in its best sense — attractive in style, clear in exposition, and eminently instructive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not be a mere compilation; should be dominated by a large, original purpose kept steadily in view throughout a close and trenchant argument. Style and clarity that render complex subject-matter accessible to non-specialists are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value as an authoritative treatment in its field
rubrics_metrics.description: A book should be "a valuable exposition" of its subject, treating a wide range of questions instructively and serving as an authoritative text-book on the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should coordinate facts in a rational conception, contribute usefully to ongoing controversies, and be executed with such learning and ability that it takes rank as an authoritative resource for both specialists and educated readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical production, illustrations, and binding quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of manufacture: "got up in elegant form... contains a large number of beautifully executed illustrations... Press-work and binding are in the best style."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality illustrations, charts, press-work and binding enhance a book's value and accessibility; these production qualities are cited as credit to publisher and author and as contributing to usefulness and attractiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook practicality — experiments and apparatus depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical manual should have a "great number of simple illustrative experiments" and a "profusion of cuts representing apparatus and manipulations".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize illustrative experiments and visual depictions of apparatus to aid lecturers and workers; practical, demonstrable examples are a primary claim to consideration for laboratory or teaching manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook attention to applied/manufacturing topics and specialized subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong manual gives prominence to manufacturing processes and practical applications (e.g., "prominence...to the subject of manufacturing processes" and attention to properties of explosives in a chemistry text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear explanations of principles behind important manufacturing processes, and coverage of specialized applied topics relevant to the author's institutional affiliations or expertise; such coverage increases usefulness to students and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-article structural standards (Pharmacographia main sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drug/article should contain the main sections: "Botanical Origin," "History," "Collection," "Description," "Microscopic Structure," "Chemical Composition," "Production and Commerce," "Uses, Adulterations, and Substitutes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this sectional template so each entry is comprehensive: taxonomic and origin data, historical use, collection/manufacture notes, physical and microscopic description, chemical composition with literature synthesis, production/commerce statistics, and practical notes on uses and adulterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-content standards and scope (Pharmacographia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should give botanical names and synonyms, exclude over-detailed botanical descriptions when inappropriate, provide unique historical accounts, explain collection/manufacture when it bears on physical properties, and carefully sift investigators' views on chemical composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide copious references to original sources; include production, cultivation, and commerce data; keep 'Adulterations and Substitutes' concise but rely on sufficient familiarity with the pure article for detection; aim for breadth and authoritative synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for illustrative support in descriptive and microscopic sections
rubrics_metrics.description: A noted desideratum is "the want of illustrations in the sections of 'Description' and 'Microscopical Structure'" for a pharmacognosy/reference work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear cuts/figures in descriptive and microscopic sections to aid identification and detection of adulteration; where lacking, refer readers to illustrated alternatives or translations that supply images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidebook criteria for health/spa travel works
rubrics_metrics.description: A satisfactory watering-place guide "described the medicinal properties of the different waters, whether for bathing or drinking, so that the intelligent reader may clearly perceive not only why he is to visit a particular watering-place, but also how he is to enter upon his treatment when he arrives there."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide rules of life and diet for treatment, maps showing places and routes, a keyed/color-coded indication of spring types, comparative currency tables, analysis of waters, a therapeutical recapitulation of special uses, and illustrations of principal places so the visitor can plan and execute treatment intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical/scholarly tone and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophical works should exhibit "calm, philosophic temper, liberality of thought, and acuteness and force of reasoning," accept relevant scientific conclusions, and address underlying foundations (psychology, nature and limits of knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid flippancy, invective or controversial abuse; present a close, logical examination and show how science affects traditional formulations, thereby serving as suitable texts for students of modern speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygiene/public-health handbook comprehensiveness and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: A hygiene handbook should "consider a large number of subjects, giving the latest and most authentic knowledge in an interesting form," with full treatment of food (function, constituents, nutritive value, dietaries), air impurities and ventilation, water impurities and detection, sewage removal and purification, and other matters relating to healthy living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised/updated editions should add recent developments (e.g., new introductory historical sketches); the book should be sufficiently practical to belong in every household and to assist physicians advising patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amateur astronomy manual requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: A manual for amateurs should "supply the materials for the study of double stars in a convenient form," including a catalogue of stars, extensive lists of measures, and up-to-date notes bringing measures to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed previous measures (with instruments, apertures, micrometers), guidance on what stars are of special interest or need observations at particular times, and indicate which stars are sufficiently measured that they currently need no attention; warn that orbit construction requires mathematical expertise and give guidance accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biography evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A good biography "delineation is instructive and entertaining," reproduces correspondence that sheds light on habits and opinions, and aims to make a just estimate of character as a man and thinker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include personal particulars that give interest, summarize leading conceptions of the subject's work, and candidly note deficiencies and the influence of contemporaneous intellectual movements to help readers gauge the subject's contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polemic works — demand for constructive originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical polemics may contain "much ingenious criticism of modern scientific doctrines," but should do more than refute—ideally they should "bring forward new theories" that withstand criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism alone is easier than proposing robust alternative theories; evaluators judge polemical works lower if they fail to present new, defensible explanations of the phenomena under dispute.
